suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Missing optional chaining on mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration crashes booking creation when destinationCalendar is null/empty.
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` is accessed without optional chaining, but `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is `undefined` whenever `evt.destinationCalendar` is null or an empty array (handleNewBooking sets it to `null` when no destination calendar exists). WHY: any booking whose location is Google Meet and that has no destination calendar now throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'integration')`, aborting the whole booking creation — previously `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration` evaluated to `undefined` and safely fell back to Cal Video. HOW: restore optional chaining: `if (evt.location === MeetLocationType && mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration !== "google_calendar")`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Video (non-calendar) results now persist credentialId: undefined in booking references, so video meetings are never deleted on cancellation.
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: for non-calendar (video) results, `credentialId` is now hardcoded to `undefined` instead of `result.credentialId`. WHY: booking references for video meetings are persisted without credentialId, and downstream deletion in handleCancelBooking.ts (line 491) requires `bookingVideoReference.credentialId` to locate the credential and call `deleteMeeting` — video meetings for bookings created after this change are never deleted on cancel/reschedule. HOW: restore the video branch: `credentialId: isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : result.credentialId` (i.e. just `credentialId: result.credentialId`).

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The fallback `find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` compares against the already-falsy externalCalendarId, so it never matches and updates are sent with calendarId: undefined.
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: in the fallback branch, `find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` compares each calendar's externalId against `externalCalendarId`, which is guaranteed falsy in that branch — the find can never match, so `selectedCalendar` is always `undefined` and `calendarId: undefined` is sent to `calendar.events.update` (line 261). WHY: updates/reschedules of Google events whose booking reference lacks externalCalendarId now fail (previously they correctly fell back to `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`); the identical pattern in deleteEvent (lines 315-317) silently degrades to the "primary" calendar, so events on non-primary calendars are never deleted (404 is swallowed at line 335). HOW: fall back to the first destination calendar instead: `const selectedCalendar = externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.[0]?.externalId;` (same for deleteEvent's calendarId).

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` silently no-ops when destinationCalendar is null, so collective team members never receive calendar events.
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` uses optional chaining on a value that was explicitly initialized to `null` (lines 1063-1067) when the organizer/eventType has no destination calendar. WHY: for collective events where the organizer has no destination calendar but team members do, the collected teamDestinationCalendars are silently dropped and no calendar events are created for any team member — the multi-host invitation feature this PR adds silently fails in exactly that scenario. HOW: initialize to an empty array instead of null (`: []` at line 1067) or use `(evt.destinationCalendar ??= []).push(...teamDestinationCalendars)`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: updateLocation's referencesToCreate drops the destinationCalendar credentialId fallback, and CalendarManager.updateEvent never returns credentialId, so new references persist credentialId NULL.
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: `credentialId: result.credentialId ?? undefined` dropped the old `?? evt.destinationCalendar?.credentialId` fallback, but `updateEvent` in CalendarManager never sets credentialId on its result (verified: only createEvent returns it), so calendar references built by updateLocation always carry credentialId undefined. WHY: editLocation.handler.ts creates new booking references from these objects, permanently losing the credential link; subsequent cancellations/updates of that booking can no longer identify the correct calendar credential and fall back to blindly hitting every calendar credential the user owns. HOW: have CalendarManager.updateEvent include `credentialId: credential.id` in its returned EventResult (mirroring createEvent), or restore the destinationCalendar[0] fallback here.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The recurring-event deletion block now runs once per calendar reference but ignores the loop's reference, causing duplicate deletions while only ever deleting each booking's first calendar reference.
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: the recurring-event deletion branch sits inside the new per-reference loop yet ignores the loop variable: it re-iterates all user calendar credentials and deletes only `updBooking.references.find(...)` (the FIRST calendar reference) of each updated booking, once per outer reference. WHY: with multiple calendar references per booking (which this PR introduces for collective events), the same events are deleted N times redundantly, and the other hosts' calendar events for recurring bookings are never deleted at all. HOW: hoist the recurring branch out of the per-reference loop and iterate all calendar references of each updated booking (`updBooking.references.filter(...)`), or delete per-reference uid with the reference's own credential/externalCalendarId.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The integration-type fallback path calls createEvent without the destination's externalId, so the stored reference loses externalCalendarId and later Google updates/deletes target the wrong calendar.
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: `createEvent(c, event)` in the no-credentialId branch doesn't pass `destination.externalId`, unlike the credentialId branch (line 370). WHY: the resulting booking reference gets `externalCalendarId: undefined` (line 169), so every later update/delete of that event can't address the calendar it was actually created on — Google updates then fail with an undefined calendarId and deletes fall back to "primary". Previously the reference stored `evt.destinationCalendar?.externalId` for this path. HOW: pass the externalId through: `destinationCalendarCredentials.map(async (c) => await createEvent(c, event, destination.externalId))`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: updateAllCalendarEvents calls updateEvent with an undefined credential when the DB lookup fails, unlike the create path which guards with `if (credential)`.
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: after the credential DB-fetch fallback, `result.push(updateEvent(credential, ...))` runs unconditionally even when `credential` is still undefined (credential not found among user credentials and missing/deleted in DB). WHY: getCalendar(undefined) throws, the surrounding catch converts the entire updateAllCalendarEvents call into failure results for every reference, so one stale reference breaks updates of all calendars; the create path added in this same PR correctly guards with `if (credential)`. HOW: wrap the push in `if (credential) { result.push(updateEvent(credential, event, bookingRefUid, calenderExternalId)); }`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: EventManager.ts:119 dereferences mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration without a null/empty guard, which throws when destinationCalendar is null or the array is empty.
suggestions.suggestionContent: At EventManager.ts:119 the expression mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration is dereferenced unconditionally. When destinationCalendar is null or the refactored destinationCalendar array is empty, mainHostDestinationCalendar is undefined/null and this line throws a TypeError at runtime (a crash bug). Add a null/empty guard before accessing .integration (or use optional chaining with an explicit fallback path). Note: the reviewer classified this as a crash bug rather than a secret/identity comparison defect, but it is the one concrete defect explicitly described.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: New loadUsers catch block forwards raw Prisma error messages into a client-facing 400 response, exposing internal schema/query details.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The new catch block re-throws PrismaClientKnownRequestError as an HttpError with the raw `error.message` sent to the client. Prisma error messages can disclose internal schema details (constraint names, field names, operation causes). Do not forward `error.message` for Prisma errors — log it server-side and return a generic message (e.g. "Unable to load users"), the same treatment the generic branch already gives non-Prisma errors.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Missing optional chaining on destructured destinationCalendar causes a TypeError crash for Google Meet bookings with no destination calendar, where the old code safely fell back to Cal Video.
suggestions.suggestionContent: `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` yields `undefined` when `evt.destinationCalendar` is null (handleNewBooking explicitly sets it to `null` when neither eventType nor organizerUser has a destination calendar), and the next line accesses `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` without optional chaining → TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined. The old code used `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration`, which safely fell back to Cal Video. Any booking with location = Google Meet and no destination calendar now crashes during event creation. Fix: `if (evt.location === MeetLocationType && mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration !== "google_calendar")`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The no-externalCalendarId fallback in updateEvent finds a calendar by equality with the falsy externalCalendarId itself, so it always resolves to undefined instead of the destination calendar's externalId as before.
suggestions.suggestionContent: In updateEvent, the fallback branch of `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` is logically dead: it only runs when externalCalendarId is falsy (null/undefined/""), yet the find predicate compares `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId`, which can never match a real calendar record. Previously the fallback was `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`, so updates to bookings whose reference lacks externalCalendarId (e.g. legacy bookings; EventManager.updateAllCalendarEvents passes `calenderExternalId = null` then) still targeted the destination calendar. Now the update is issued with `calendarId: undefined` and the event is not updated on the real calendar. The fallback should select the destination calendar directly, e.g. `event.destinationCalendar?.[0]?.externalId` (or find by credentialId), not by equality with the already-known-falsy externalCalendarId.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: deleteEvent's fallback find compares against the already-falsy externalCalendarId, so it always yields undefined and deletes from no calendar when the booking reference lacks an externalCalendarId.
suggestions.suggestionContent: deleteEvent repeats the same dead fallback as updateEvent: `const calendarId = externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;`. In the else branch externalCalendarId is falsy, so the find predicate compares calendar externalIds against null/"" and always returns undefined, whereas the old code fell back to `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`. Cancellation of bookings whose reference has no externalCalendarId (handleCancelBooking passes the reference's nullable externalCalendarId) will issue the delete with an undefined calendarId and fail to remove the event from the organizer's actual calendar. Use the destination calendar's externalId (e.g. `event.destinationCalendar?.[0]?.externalId`) as the fallback.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: When no destination calendar matches the credentialId (e.g. entries with null credentialId), createEvent silently targets "primary" instead of the destination calendar the old code used.
suggestions.suggestionContent: createEvent now resolves the target calendar with `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)?.externalId` and silently falls back to "primary". For destination calendar entries without a credentialId (a case EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents explicitly handles by fanning out to every credential of the integration), the lookup can never match, so the event is created on the user's primary calendar instead of the destination calendar's externalId that the old code used directly. Consider falling back to the first destination calendar's externalId before "primary" so events don't silently land on the wrong calendar.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Google Meet fallback dereferences `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` which is `undefined` whenever `evt.destinationCalendar` is null/empty, crashing booking creation.
suggestions.suggestionContent: When `evt.destinationCalendar` is null or `[]` (handleNewBooking now sets it to `null` when neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar), `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` yields `undefined`, and line 119 accesses `.integration` without optional chaining. For any booking whose location is Google Meet with no destination calendar set, this throws an unhandled TypeError inside EventManager.create() instead of falling back to Cal Video as before. Restore the safe access: `if (evt.location === MeetLocationType && mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration !== "google_calendar")`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Video (non-calendar) booking references are now persisted with credentialId: undefined instead of result.credentialId, breaking later update/delete of the video meeting.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The mapping was changed from `credentialId: isCalendarType ? evt.destinationCalendar?.credentialId : result.credentialId` to `credentialId: isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : undefined`. Every video result (Daily, etc.) now produces a reference with credentialId `undefined`. These referencesToCreate are written to the booking's BookingReference rows; cancel/reschedule flows (e.g., handleCancelBooking, video deletion) look up the integration credential via reference.credentialId, so all video references created after this change permanently lose the link to the video credential and the meeting can no longer be updated/deleted. Use `result.credentialId` for both branches.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: updateEvent/deleteEvent fallback `find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` can never match when externalCalendarId is null, yielding an undefined calendarId and a Google API 'Missing required parameters' error.
suggestions.suggestionContent: In both updateEvent (lines 254-256) and deleteEvent (lines 314-317) the new fallback is `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`. When `externalCalendarId` is null/empty — which happens for bookings whose reference has `externalCalendarId: null` (legacy bookings; handleCancelBooking passes the reference value straight through to deleteEvent) — the predicate compares each calendar's externalId against null and can never match, so `selectedCalendar`/`calendarId` becomes `undefined` and the google client raises `Missing required parameters: calendarId`. The old code fell back to `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`. Use the first destination as the fallback instead: `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.[0]?.externalId`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Office365 (and lark/CalDAV) always target destinationCalendar[0].externalId — for COLLECTIVE team events a member's credential is used to write into the organizer's calendar id, causing 404s or cross-calendar writes.
suggestions.suggestionContent: handleNewBooking now builds `evt.destinationCalendar` as [eventType/organizer calendar, ...team members' calendars], and EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents loops every destination and calls createEvent with each member's own credential. GoogleCalendarService was updated to pick the destination matching the credentialId, but Office365 (here), larkcalendar, and the CalDAV base service still destructure `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []` and use the FIRST element's externalId regardless of which credential is executing. For a collective event with an Office365-using team member, the member's `/me/calendars/{organizerExternalId}/events` call targets a calendar id that does not exist in the member's mailbox → 404 (silently swallowed as success=false) or a wrong-calendar write. Match the destination by credential like Google does (createEvent receives credential.id) or pass the per-destination externalId through to the service.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Google Meet bookings with no destination calendar now crash with a TypeError instead of falling back to Cal Video.
suggestions.suggestionContent: When `destinationCalendar` became an array, this consumer was rewritten but lost its null-safety: `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is `undefined` whenever `evt.destinationCalendar` is null or empty, so `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` throws a TypeError. This hits exactly the case the fallback was written for — Google Meet selected without any destination/Google calendar (handleNewBooking sets `destinationCalendar: null` in that case) — so the booking now crashes instead of falling back to Cal Video. Restore the optional chain: `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration !== "google_calendar"`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: updateEvent/deleteEvent lost the fallback to the destination calendar — the new find() predicate compares against a value that is falsy by construction, so it can never match.
suggestions.suggestionContent: In the fallback branch `externalCalendarId` is falsy by construction (the ternary already handled the truthy case), so `find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` can never match a real destination calendar — the previous fallback `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` was effectively deleted. Event updates for booking references without an `externalCalendarId` (older bookings, or references created through paths that don't pass externalId) now go out with `calendarId: undefined` instead of the destination calendar. Match by credentialId like createEvent does (or fall back to the first destination calendar's externalId), e.g. `: event.destinationCalendar?.[0]?.externalId`. The same dead predicate was introduced in deleteEvent at lines 314-317, where it silently retargets deletes to 'primary' — fix both.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Collective team members' destination calendars are silently dropped when the organizer/event type has no destination calendar, because `evt.destinationCalendar` is null and `?.push` no-ops.
suggestions.suggestionContent: When the organizer and event type both lack a destination calendar, `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null` (set a few lines above), so `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` silently drops every collective team member's calendar — the new array contract needs the array initialized here, not just guarded. Use `evt.destinationCalendar = [...(evt.destinationCalendar ?? []), ...teamDestinationCalendars]` so members still get calendar events when the organizer has none.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: updateEvent's fallback searches destinationCalendar for cal.externalId === externalCalendarId, but that branch only runs when externalCalendarId is falsy, so the find can never match.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The `find` predicate compares `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId`, but this branch only executes when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so it can never match and always returns undefined. Fall back to the destination calendar's externalId directly, as the old code did.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: deleteEvent's calendarId fallback has the same impossible predicate: it only runs when externalCalendarId is falsy yet searches for a calendar whose externalId equals that falsy value.
suggestions.suggestionContent: Same dead condition as updateEvent: the fallback `.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` can never match because the branch requires externalCalendarId to be falsy. Fall back to the destination calendar's externalId directly.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is undefined when evt.destinationCalendar is null/empty, and accessing `.integration` without optional chaining throws when the location is Google Meet.
suggestions.suggestionContent: When `evt.destinationCalendar` is null, `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is undefined and `.integration` throws. Add optional chaining so the Google-Meet-without-Google-Calendar fallback keeps working.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: In the no-credentialId branch, createEvent is called without destination.externalId, so the stored booking reference gets externalCalendarId undefined even though the event was created in destination.externalId.
suggestions.suggestionContent: This branch creates the event in `destination.externalId`'s calendar but never passes it to createEvent, so `result.externalId` (and the persisted `externalCalendarId`) is undefined. Pass the externalId through, matching the branch above.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: isTeamAdminOrOwner uses && so only team OWNERS pass, blocking team admins from adding guests.
suggestions.suggestionContent:
WHAT: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...)` even though `isTeamAdmin` already returns truthy for both ADMIN and OWNER roles (packages/lib/server/queries/teams/index.ts:264-284, OR: [{ role: "ADMIN" }, { role: "OWNER" }]) while `isTeamOwner` is true only for OWNER.
WHY: The AND collapses the check to OWNER-only, so a team admin (non-owner) attempting to add guests to a team booking always hits the FORBIDDEN branch at line 54 — the feature is broken for team admins.
HOW: Replace with `const isTeamAdminOrOwner = await isTeamAdmin(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0);` (isTeamAdmin already covers owners) or use `||` if both helpers are kept.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Any attendee of a booking can add an unbounded list of guests, turning the endpoint into a spam relay that leaks meeting details.
suggestions.suggestionContent:
WHAT: The handler authorizes any existing attendee (`isAttendee`, line 52) to add guests, and the input schema `z.array(z.string().email())` places no upper bound on the number of guests per request (addGuests.schema.ts:5), with no rate limiting on the mutation.
WHY: Any person invited to a meeting can submit an arbitrary number of guest emails; each one is persisted as an attendee and sent an AttendeeScheduledEmail containing the event title, location and video-conference URL — a spam/abuse vector and disclosure of meeting details to arbitrary third parties, plus repeated organizer/attendee notification emails on every call.
HOW: Cap the array (e.g. `guests: z.array(z.string().email()).max(10)`), restrict the permission to organizer/team admin-or-owner (drop the isAttendee branch if attendee-added guests are not a product requirement), and consider per-booking/per-user rate limiting on the mutation.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Server schema does not enforce guest uniqueness, so a direct API call creates duplicate attendee rows.
suggestions.suggestionContent:
WHAT: The uniqueness refine for guest emails exists only in the client dialog (AddGuestsDialog.tsx:26-29); the server-side `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` is a plain `z.array(z.string().email())` and the handler's `uniqueGuests` filter (handler lines 74-78) only dedupes against already-stored attendees, not within the submitted array.
WHY: A direct tRPC request with `guests: ["a@b.com", "a@b.com"]` passes validation and `createMany` inserts two identical Attendee rows (no unique constraint on bookingId+email); two concurrent requests also both pass the existence check before either writes (TOCTOU).
HOW: Add a uniqueness refine/transform to the server schema (e.g. `.refine((emails) => new Set(emails.map(e => e.toLowerCase())).size === emails.length)`) or dedupe `uniqueGuests` in the handler before createMany.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Blacklist and duplicate-attendee checks are case-sensitive on the guest side, so case variants bypass both.
suggestions.suggestionContent:
WHAT: `blacklistedGuestEmails` entries are lowercased (line 71) but `guest` is compared un-lowercased in both `blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` and `guest === attendee.email`.
WHY: Submitting a blacklisted address with different casing (e.g. `Blocked@Domain.com`) bypasses the blacklist entirely, and an existing attendee's email with different casing passes the duplicate check, creating a second attendee row for the same person.
HOW: Normalize once, e.g. `const normalizedGuest = guest.toLowerCase()` (or lowercase in the schema via `.transform()`), and compare `attendee.email.toLowerCase()` on the other side.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: EventManager is built with the calling user's credentials instead of the organizer's, so calendar updates can target the wrong user's calendar when the caller is an attendee.
suggestions.suggestionContent:
WHAT: `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` (line 158) loads the session user's credentials and builds the EventManager with `...user` (the caller), even though the calendar/video references on the booking belong to the organizer (`booking.userId`).
WHY: The handler explicitly allows attendees and team admins to add guests; in EventManager.updateAllCalendarEvents, references without a credentialId are resolved by filtering the manager's credentials by reference type (packages/core/EventManager.ts:871-878) — with an attendee caller this targets the attendee's own calendar credentials (wrong user's event, or a silent no-op when they have none), so the organizer's calendar event never gets the new guest.
HOW: Build the EventManager from the organizer (`booking.user`, already included in the query) and the organizer's credentials instead of `ctx.user`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: sendAddGuestsEmails is passed the raw `guests` input instead of `uniqueGuests`, so pre-existing attendees included in the input receive the wrong (new-guest) email.
suggestions.suggestionContent:
WHAT: `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` passes the unfiltered input array, while the handler already computed `uniqueGuests` (lines 74-78) excluding emails that are already attendees.
WHY: In sendAddGuestsEmails (packages/emails/email-manager.ts:541), any attendee whose email appears in `newGuests` is sent the new-guest `AttendeeScheduledEmail`; an existing attendee who was (redundantly) included in the request therefore receives a fresh "you are scheduled" invite instead of the "guests added" notification — confusing and regenerates a booking confirmation for someone who was already booked.
HOW: Pass `uniqueGuests` instead of `guests`: `await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, uniqueGuests);`

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: sendAddGuestsEmails ignores the event type's disableHostEmail/disableAttendeeEmail settings unlike the sibling sendLocationChangeEmails.
suggestions.suggestionContent:
WHAT: `sendAddGuestsEmails` unconditionally emails the organizer, team members, and all attendees, whereas the adjacent `sendLocationChangeEmails` gates those same sends behind `eventTypeDisableHostEmail(eventTypeMetadata)` and `eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail(eventTypeMetadata)`.
WHY: Event types configured to suppress host or attendee emails (an existing product setting) will still emit these new add-guests notifications, silently overriding the user's email preferences.
HOW: Accept the event-type metadata (available via booking.eventType in the handler) and apply the same `eventTypeDisableHostEmail` / `eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail` guards before pushing the respective emails.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: findFirstOrThrow with `booking.userId || 0` throws an unhandled 500 for bookings without a userId.
suggestions.suggestionContent:
WHAT: The organizer is fetched with `prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } })` even though the initial booking query already included `user` (lines 35-40).
WHY: For bookings with `userId = null` (possible for team bookings), the `|| 0` fallback matches no row and findFirstOrThrow throws, producing an unhandled 500 instead of a clean NOT_FOUND/FORBIDDEN; the extra round trip is also unnecessary when the organizer row is already loaded as `booking.user`.
HOW: Use `booking.user` from the first query and throw a TRPCError (e.g. NOT_FOUND) when it is null.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Blacklist emails are lowercased but incoming guest emails are compared against them un-normalized, allowing case-variation bypass of the BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS control.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The blacklist entries are normalized with toLowerCase() (line 71) but the incoming guest emails are checked with `blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` without any normalization (line 77). Since email comparison is case-insensitive, a guest submitted as `Blocked@Example.com` bypasses a blacklist containing `blocked@example.com`. Normalize the guest (e.g. `guest.trim().toLowerCase()`) before the includes() check so both sides of the comparison use the same casing.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Duplicate-attendee detection compares guest and attendee emails with raw === so case variants of the same mailbox are added as duplicate attendees.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The deduplication check `guest === attendee.email` (line 76) performs a case-sensitive comparison on case-insensitive email identity with no normalization on either side. Submitting `Guest@Example.com` when `guest@example.com` is already an attendee passes the filter and creates a duplicate attendee for the same mailbox (the client-side Set-based uniqueness check in AddGuestsDialog.tsx is likewise case-sensitive). Compare normalized values, e.g. `guest.trim().toLowerCase() === attendee.email.toLowerCase()`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Filtered `uniqueGuests` is computed but the raw unfiltered `guests` is passed to sendAddGuestsEmails, misclassifying existing attendees as new guests.
suggestions.suggestionContent: Line 74-78 computes `uniqueGuests` (excluding emails already on the booking and blacklisted emails) and uses it for the DB write, but line 168 calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` with the original unfiltered array. In email-manager.ts, `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` is the branch key that decides whether an attendee receives AttendeeScheduledEmail (a fresh 'you are booked' confirmation) or AttendeeAddGuestsEmail (a 'guests were added' notification). An email submitted that is already an attendee therefore receives the wrong email template. Pass `uniqueGuests` instead of `guests`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed with `&&` although the name (and the permission gate using it) declares admin OR owner.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The variable is named `isTeamAdminOrOwner` but is computed as `isTeamAdmin(user.id, teamId) && isTeamOwner(user.id, teamId)`. With AND semantics, a team admin who is not also the team owner (a normal configuration) fails the permission check at line 54 and receives FORBIDDEN when trying to add guests, contradicting the declared 'Or' intent and the OR semantics used by sibling booking handlers (e.g. editLocation). Use `||` so either role is authorized.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Blacklist entries are lowercased at the write site but the guest email is not lowercased at the read site, so mixed-case blacklisted emails bypass the check.
suggestions.suggestionContent: Line 71 normalizes the blacklist with `.map((email) => email.toLowerCase())`, but line 77 tests `blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` against the raw `guest` string. The two sides of the comparison disagree on case normalization, so `BadActor@Example.com` is not matched against a blacklist containing `badactor@example.com` and is added as a guest. Lowercase `guest` before the `includes` check (and ideally before the attendee duplicate comparison on line 76 as well).

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The `|| t("unable_to_add_guests")` fallback can never execute because the template-literal `message` is always a non-empty string.
suggestions.suggestionContent: `const message = `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`;` always produces a non-empty string (at minimum 'undefined: ...'), so `showToast(message || t("unable_to_add_guests"), "error")` has a dead fallback branch — the 'unable_to_add_guests' text is unreachable. Either drop the fallback or build `message` conditionally so the generic text is shown when `err.message` is absent.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The 'Remove email' tooltip is hardcoded English while every other string in this component goes through useLocale().t().
suggestions.suggestionContent: The Tooltip content "Remove email" is a hardcoded English string shown to users, bypassing the translation mechanism. The same file imports useLocale and translates its other user-facing string (t("add_another") at line 69), and the label is passed in already-translated by the caller, so this tooltip will remain untranslated for non-English users. No translation key for it was added to common.json in this PR. Fix: use t("remove_email") (and add the key) or a comparable existing key.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Variable named isTeamAdminOrOwner is computed with && (admin AND owner), so the name states a disjunction the code does not implement.
suggestions.suggestionContent: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...)` — the name promises "admin OR owner" but the code requires both roles simultaneously. Read together with the guard at line 54 (`if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee)`), a team admin who is not the team owner (or an owner not flagged as admin) is denied with "you_do_not_have_permission", contradicting what the identifier — the contract a reader of the permission check relies on — says is being tested. Either the operator should be `||` to match the name (compare the neighboring pattern used elsewhere for team permission checks) or the variable should be renamed to reflect the stricter condition.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The translated fallback t("unable_to_add_guests") is dead code because `message` (a template literal) is always truthy, so users always see a raw error code prefix instead.
suggestions.suggestionContent: `message` is built with a template literal, so it is always truthy — even when err.data?.code is undefined it becomes the string "undefined: ...". The fallback `message || t("unable_to_add_guests")` can therefore never select the translated fallback, making the "unable_to_add_guests" string added to en/common.json in this PR unreachable, and the user-facing toast is always prefixed with an internal TRPC error code (e.g. "BAD_REQUEST: ..."). Fix: show the friendly message when there is no usable code, e.g. `const message = err.data?.code ? `${err.data.code}: ${t(err.message)}` : t("unable_to_add_guests");`

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The error message 'emails_must_be_unique_valid' is thrown when the submitted emails were filtered out for already being attendees or blacklisted — a condition the message does not describe.
suggestions.suggestionContent: When every submitted guest is removed by the filter at lines 74-78 (already an attendee of the booking, or on BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS), the handler throws message "emails_must_be_unique_valid" ("Emails must be unique and valid"). In that scenario the entered emails are unique and well-formed — the dialog already validated that client-side with the same message key — so the user is told their input failed a check it actually passed, with no indication the guests were already invited or blocked. Reusing one message key for two different failure conditions makes the user-facing text disagree with the code path that raises it; a distinct message such as "guests_already_added" (with a new locale key) would match the actual condition.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The error toast renders the raw server error message via t(err.message), leaking internal error details to the UI when the mutation fails with a non-keyed error.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The onError handler passes err.message through t() and shows the result in a toast. For unexpected server failures (e.g., Prisma errors from prisma.booking.update or findFirstOrThrow in addGuests.handler.ts), err.message is not an i18n key, so t() returns the raw server error string and it is rendered to the user, disclosing internal error details. Only translate known message keys and fall back to the generic copy otherwise, e.g.: const knownKeys = ["booking_not_found", "you_do_not_have_permission", "emails_must_be_unique_valid"]; const message = err.data?.code && knownKeys.includes(err.message) ? `${err.data.code}: ${t(err.message)}` : t("unable_to_add_guests"); showToast(message, "error");

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Server schema lacks the client-side uniqueness check, so one crafted request can insert duplicate Attendee rows for the same booking.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The server-side schema accepts duplicate emails within one request. The uniqueness invariant ("Emails must be unique and valid") is only enforced in the client dialog's zod refine (AddGuestsDialog.tsx:26-29), and the handler's uniqueGuests filter (addGuests.handler.ts:74-78) only removes guests that already exist as attendees — it never dedupes within the incoming array. A direct tRPC/API call with guests:["a@b.com","a@b.com"] passes validation, both entries survive the filter (neither is an existing attendee), and createMany inserts two Attendee rows with the same email on the same booking, corrupting the attendee list. Fix: add the same uniqueness refine here (e.g. `.refine((emails) => new Set(emails).size === emails.length)`) or dedupe the array in the handler before createMany.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Read-attendees-then-createMany is a TOCTOU race that lets concurrent requests insert duplicate guests.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The uniqueness check and the insert are a check-then-act sequence with no transaction or upsert: the handler reads booking.attendees (lines 26-42), filters out already-present emails (lines 74-78), and only later inserts via prisma.booking.update + createMany (lines 92-106). Two concurrent addGuests requests for the same booking containing the same new email (e.g. organizer and an attendee acting simultaneously, or a retried/double-submitted request — the dialog's loading state only blocks one client's button) both read the attendee list before either writes, both pass the filter, and both insert the same email, leaving duplicate Attendee rows. Fix: perform the dedupe-and-insert atomically (e.g. a transaction that re-checks, skipDuplicates where supported, or a unique constraint on Attendee(bookingId, email) with conflict handling).

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: findFirstOrThrow on booking.userId||0 turns bookings with a null organizer into an unhandled 500 for attendee callers.
suggestions.suggestionContent: prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow({ id: booking.userId || 0 }) throws a raw Prisma NotFoundError when booking.userId is null (Booking.userId is nullable, e.g. some team/dynamic-assignment bookings). This is reachable via the isAttendee authorization branch (line 52): an attendee of such a booking passes the permission check, then this lookup for user id 0 fails and surfaces as an unhandled 500 instead of a clean TRPCError. Fix: handle the null userId case explicitly (throw a TRPCError, or fall back to booking.user / eventType host) before calling findFirstOrThrow.

suggestions.label: logic-bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: isTeamAdminOrOwner uses && instead of ||, incorrectly locking out non-owner team admins.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The boolean guard on lines 46-48 combines isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner with && even though the variable is named isTeamAdminOrOwner. This locks out non-owner team admins who should be permitted. The conditions should be combined with || to match the name and intended behavior.

suggestions.label: behavior-bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Unfiltered `guests` is passed to sendAddGuestsEmails instead of `uniqueGuests`, causing wrong email type for duplicate guests.
suggestions.suggestionContent: Line 168 passes the unfiltered `guests` array to sendAddGuestsEmails instead of the deduplicated/filtered `uniqueGuests`. As a result, a duplicate guest who is already an attendee receives an AttendeeScheduledEmail instead of the intended AttendeeAddGuestsEmail. Pass `uniqueGuests` instead.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Handler passes the raw unfiltered `guests` input to sendAddGuestsEmails, whose `newGuests` parameter assumes the deduped newly-added set, so pre-existing attendees re-submitted as guests receive the wrong email.
suggestions.suggestionContent: email-manager.ts:525-547 (same PR) declares this parameter as `newGuests` and uses `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` to decide who gets the new-guest `AttendeeScheduledEmail` versus the `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail` notification. This handler already computes `uniqueGuests` (lines 74-78) — excluding emails already on the booking and blacklisted ones — and only those are persisted (line 101), but it then passes the raw input `guests` here. Any submitted email that already belongs to an existing attendee makes that attendee classify as a 'new guest' and receive the full scheduled/welcome email instead of the guests-added notification. Pass `uniqueGuests` instead of `guests` to match the consumer's contract.

suggestions.label: dead-code
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The `|| t(...)` fallback at line 44 is dead code because the template literal `message` is always non-empty, so the fallback branch can never run.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The `message || t(...)` fallback at line 44 is dead code: the template literal assigned to `message` is always non-empty, so the `|| t(...)` branch can never execute. The reviewer notes this is harmless (it misclassifies no legitimate falsy data), but the unreachable fallback can be removed for clarity.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The zod safeParse result object `{ success, data }` is stored as the Google credential key instead of the parsed token data.
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the zod `SafeParseReturnType` (`{ success: true, data: ... }`), and line 97 assigns that whole object to `key`, which is then persisted as the credential's key. WHY: after the first token refresh the stored key becomes `{ success, data }`, so the next service construction (`googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` at line 75) throws and the Google Calendar credential is permanently broken — previously `googleCredentialSchema.parse()` returned the bare parsed object. HOW: store `parsedKey.data` (after checking `.success`) instead of the wrapper object, matching how office365calendar/zoom consume the same helper.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The freshly refreshed Salesforce access token is saved to the DB but the jsforce.Connection is still built with the old, possibly expired token.
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: the new refresh block obtains and persists a new Salesforce access token, but the `jsforce.Connection` is still initialized with the old `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url`. WHY: every calendar operation runs on the stale (potentially expired) token even though a valid one was just fetched, and the old `refresh_token` is both re-stored and handed to jsforce even though the manual refresh may have rotated it — breaking jsforce's own fallback refresh. HOW: build the Connection with `accessTokenParsed.data.access_token` / `accessTokenParsed.data.instance_url`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: `credentialId` is passed as the `userId` argument to refreshOAuthTokens, so the sync endpoint receives the credential ID as the Cal.com user ID.
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: the third argument to `refreshOAuthTokens` is `credentialId`, but the parameter is `userId: number | null` and is sent to the sync endpoint as `calcomUserId`. WHY: when credential sync is enabled, the parent application receives the credential's primary key instead of the user's ID, so it refreshes/posts tokens for the wrong (or a non-existent) user — every other caller (zohocrm, google, hubspot, etc.) correctly passes `credential.userId`. HOW: thread `credential.userId` into `refreshAccessToken` and pass it instead of `credentialId`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The credential-sync branch returns the raw fetch Response without parsing the body, but several updated callers consume the result as an already-parsed token object.
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: in the sync branch the helper returns the unparsed fetch `Response`, while google (`res?.data`), hubspot (`hubspotRefreshToken.expiresIn/accessToken`), zoho-bigin (`tokenInfo.data.error`) and zohocrm (`zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error`) use the return value as a parsed token payload. WHY: with credential sync enabled, token refresh for these apps either throws (`.data` on a Response is undefined) or silently stores NaN/undefined tokens, so the feature is broken for exactly the calendar apps it targets. HOW: either `await response.json()` inside the helper before returning, or update the affected callers to parse the Response body.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: `appStoreMetadata` is keyed by app directory name (e.g. `googlecalendar`) but is indexed with the DB app slug (e.g. `google-calendar`), so the webhook 404s for hyphenated apps.
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: `appStoreMetadata[app.slug]` looks up metadata by the DB slug, but the generated metadata map is keyed by app directory name (`googlecalendar`, `office365calendar`, `larkcalendar`, `office365video`) while DB slugs are `google-calendar`, `office365-calendar`, `lark-calendar`, `msteams`. WHY: for every hyphenated app the metadata lookup returns undefined and the webhook responds 404 "App not found", so credential sync fails for the primary calendar/video apps even though the App row exists. HOW: find the metadata entry whose own `slug` property matches `app.slug` (e.g. `Object.values(appStoreMetadata).find(m => m.slug === app.slug)`) instead of using the slug as a key.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: `minimumTokenResponseSchema`'s computed keys (`[z.string().toString()]`) collapse to the literal "[object Object]", so the expiry field is never captured and zod strips everything except `access_token`.
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: the "any number property is the expiry" index signature does not work — both computed keys evaluate to the literal string "[object Object]", so the schema is effectively `{ access_token: string, "[object Object]": unknown? }`. WHY: when credential sharing is enabled, the parsed result keeps only `access_token` (zod strips unknown keys), the expiry the endpoint returns is discarded (office365calendar then merges data with an old `expiry_date`, causing an immediate re-expiry/refresh loop), and a placeholder `refresh_token: "refresh_token"` is persisted into the credential. HOW: use `.catchall(z.unknown())` (or `z.record`) on a plain `{ access_token: z.string() }` object and copy the real expiry field explicitly.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The new team branch creates team-scoped OAuth credentials for any accepted team member, while the admin-access guard is only invoked (as a no-op with null teamId) in the user path.
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: when `state.teamId` is present, the code only checks that the caller is an accepted member of the team before creating a team-scoped credential; it never verifies admin/owner role. WHY: any regular team member can install OAuth app credentials on behalf of the whole team — the existing `throwIfNotHaveAdminAccessToTeam` guard (which enforces admin access) is only called in the non-team branch with `teamId: null`, where it immediately returns. HOW: call `throwIfNotHaveAdminAccessToTeam({ teamId: state.teamId, userId })` inside the team branch (replacing or in addition to the membership check).

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The findFirst-then-create sequence races: two concurrent webhook calls for the same user/app both find no credential and both insert duplicates.
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: the webhook does `findFirst` then `create` without a unique constraint or transaction, so concurrent requests for the same `(userId, appId)` both observe no credential and both insert. WHY: duplicate credential rows for the same user/app cause ambiguous credential selection downstream (Cal.com picks one arbitrarily) and desync from the parent platform. HOW: add a unique index on `(userId, appId)` and use `prisma.credential.upsert`, or catch the unique-violation and fall back to update.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: parseRefreshTokenResponse now throws on an unparseable token response where the previous code logged the error and continued with the existing credentials.
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` throws when Microsoft's 200 response fails schema validation, replacing the previous behavior of logging the zod error and continuing with the existing credentials. WHY: a single malformed-but-successful token response now rejects `getToken()` and fails all Office365 calendar operations for that credential instead of degrading gracefully as before. HOW: either catch the helper's error in `refreshAccessToken` and log it (restoring the old tolerance), or make the helper return the safeParse result without throwing.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the zod safeParse wrapper `{success, data}`, but this consumer stores it directly as the credential key, corrupting every Google credential on refresh.
suggestions.suggestionContent: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the zod safeParse result wrapper ({ success, data }), not the parsed credential object (it calls schema.safeParse, see packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:18,29). Storing it directly as `key` writes `{ success: true, data: {...} }` into the credential table, and the next `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` (line 75) then throws — the credential is corrupted after its first refresh. Unwrap `.data` before persisting, matching how office365calendar and salesforce consume the same helper.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: When credential sharing is enabled, refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response, but this consumer still reads `res?.data` (gaxios shape), so token refresh throws and is silently swallowed.
suggestions.suggestionContent: refreshOAuthTokens returns two different shapes depending on config: the refreshFunction's return value (here a gaxios response with `.data`) or a raw fetch `Response` when credential sharing is enabled (refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8-15). This consumer only handles the gaxios shape — `res?.data` is undefined for a fetch Response and the body is never read via `res.json()`, so in sync mode line 95 (`token.access_token`) throws a TypeError that the surrounding catch swallows, silently leaving an expired access token. Normalize both branches (e.g. parse the fetch Response with `.json()`) before reading the token fields.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Truthiness check on `refresh_token` replaces a missing token with the literal string "refresh_token", which overwrites and permanently corrupts the stored credential in callers that spread the parsed data over existing keys.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The truthiness test `!refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token` treats a missing (or empty-string) refresh_token as license to inject the literal string "refresh_token" into the parsed result. Callers that merge the parsed data over the existing credential key (office365calendar: `{ ...o365AuthCredentials, ...tokenResponse.data }`) then overwrite the real refresh token with that sentinel and persist it, permanently breaking the integration on the next refresh. Restrict the placeholder to the credential-sync branch where it is actually required, or keep it out of the object returned to callers.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Comments claim the zod schema captures any numeric property as the expiry and allows other properties, but z.object with computed keys does neither — unknown fields are stripped.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The comments on this schema describe behaviour the code does not have. `z.object` does not support catch-all keys: `[z.string().toString()]` evaluates to the literal string "[object Object]" (zod types don't override toString), so both computed entries collapse to one static key, and z.object strips unknown keys by default. Parsing a sync-endpoint response like `{access_token, expires_in: 3600, ...}` yields only `{access_token}` — the expiry the first comment says is "assumed" is silently discarded, and "other properties" are not allowed through either. The comments should be removed/rewritten (and if pass-through of expiry is intended, this needs `.catchall()`/`.passthrough()` — which it currently does not do).

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The safeParse result wrapper {success, data} is stored as the credential key instead of the parsed tokens, permanently breaking the credential after its first refresh.
suggestions.suggestionContent: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the full zod safeParse result `{ success, data }`, but this caller persists the whole object as the credential `key`. The next time the service is constructed, `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` (line 75) throws because the tokens are nested under `.data` — the credential is unrecoverable after one refresh. Use the parsed data: `const { data: key } = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema);`

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: In credential-sharing mode this returns a raw fetch Response, but callers treat the result like the SDK/axios response shape, so token refresh silently never happens.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The sharing branch returns a raw fetch `Response` while the non-sharing branch returns whatever the app's SDK/axios call returns, so every caller consumes two different shapes. E.g. Google does `res?.data` then `token.access_token` (CalendarService.ts:94-95) — with a Response, `.data` is undefined and the property read throws, which the surrounding catch swallows, so the refreshed token is never stored. Parse the body here (`return await response.json()` after a `response.ok` check) and make callers handle one consistent shape.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: In sharing mode the minimum schema strips everything but access_token and then writes the literal string "refresh_token" over the credential's real refresh token before it is persisted.
suggestions.suggestionContent: Two problems in sharing mode: (1) `minimumTokenResponseSchema`'s computed keys (`z.string().toString()`) do not create an index signature, so zod strips every field except `access_token` — the expiry is lost. (2) Lines 25-27 write the literal string `"refresh_token"` into the parsed data when the response omits one; office365calendar then spreads this over the stored credentials and persists it, permanently overwriting the real refresh token in the database. Keep the caller's existing refresh_token instead of inventing a placeholder, and model the expiry field explicitly.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Malformed bodies and undecryptable/garbage `keys` payloads throw unhandled ZodError/decrypt/JSON.parse exceptions, crashing the webhook with a 500 instead of a 4xx response.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The handler never catches: (1) `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)` at line 31 throws ZodError on an invalid body, and (2) `symmetricDecrypt` / `JSON.parse` at lines 57-59 throw when `keys` is not a valid AES-encrypted JSON payload. Both surface as unhandled 500s from a machine-to-machine webhook. Catch these and return `res.status(400).json({ message: "Invalid request body or keys" })` so the calling application gets a meaningful response.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Webhook secret is verified with a short-circuiting !== string comparison, leaking timing information about the secret prefix; use a constant-time comparison.
suggestions.suggestionContent: Webhook secret is verified with a short-circuiting !== string comparison, leaking timing information about the secret prefix; use a constant-time comparison.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: zoho-bigin passes the credential ID instead of the user ID as the calcomUserId identity sent to the credential-sync endpoint, so tokens are synced for the wrong (or nonexistent) user.
suggestions.suggestionContent: zoho-bigin passes the credential ID instead of the user ID as the calcomUserId identity sent to the credential-sync endpoint, so tokens are synced for the wrong (or nonexistent) user.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: A hardcoded literal string "refresh_token" is injected as the stored refresh token when a provider omits one, silently overwriting real refresh tokens in the credential store.
suggestions.suggestionContent: A hardcoded literal string "refresh_token" is injected as the stored refresh token when a provider omits one, silently overwriting real refresh tokens in the credential store.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Google Calendar stores the {success, data} wrapper from parseRefreshTokenResponse as the credential key instead of the parsed credentials.
suggestions.suggestionContent: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the full safeParse result object ({ success, data }) — as its other callers confirm (office365calendar uses tokenResponse.success/tokenResponse.data, salesforce uses accessTokenParsed.data). Here the wrapper itself is assigned to `key` and written to prisma.credential, replacing the old `googleCredentialSchema.parse(googleCredentials)` which stored the bare credentials object. The credential row will contain {success:true,data:{...}} instead of the Google tokens, so every subsequent read of credential.key (schema validation, access_token/refresh_token lookup) fails and Google Calendar stops working after the first token refresh. Fix: unwrap the result, e.g. `const { data: key } = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema);`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: zoho-bigin passes the credential ID where refreshOAuthTokens expects (and forwards as `calcomUserId`) the user ID.
suggestions.suggestionContent: refreshOAuthTokens' third argument is `userId` and is POSTed to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT as `calcomUserId` (refreshOAuthTokens.ts:11). Every other integration passes `credential.userId` (hubspot, lark, office365calendar, office365video, webex, zoomvideo, zohocrm, googlecalendar); this call passes `credentialId` — the Credential row's primary key — so when credential syncing is enabled the parent application receives a credential id labelled as the Cal.com user id and will sync/return tokens for the wrong (or a nonexistent) user. Pass `credential.userId` here (threading the credential object into this refresh path if needed).

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The `!accessTokenParsed.success` check is unreachable because parseRefreshTokenResponse throws on parse failure before returning.
suggestions.suggestionContent: parseRefreshTokenResponse already throws `new Error("Invalid refreshed tokens were returned")` when safeParse fails (parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:21-23), so by the time it returns, `.success` is always true. This `if (!accessTokenParsed.success) return Promise.reject(...)` branch can never execute — the intended rejection-with-message is dead code and failures instead surface as an uncaught throw from inside the helper. Either drop the check or have parseRefreshTokenResponse return the result without throwing.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Google Calendar persists the zod safeParse wrapper `{ success, data }` as the credential key because parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the wrapper, unlike the old `.parse()` call it replaced.
suggestions.suggestionContent: parseRefreshTokenResponse (packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts) returns the zod safeParse result wrapper `{ success, data }`, not the parsed credentials — it throws on failure and otherwise returns `refreshTokenResponse` unchanged. Every other consumer added in this PR (office365calendar, salesforce, zoomvideo) reads `.success`/`.data` off the return value. Here the wrapper itself is assigned to `key` and written to the database, replacing the old `googleCredentialSchema.parse(googleCredentials)` which returned unwrapped data. After the first token refresh, the stored credential key becomes `{ success: true, data: {...} }` instead of the token object, so the next read of this credential gets a malformed key and Google Calendar stops working for that user. Unwrap the result before persisting.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: zoho-bigin passes the credential row id (`credentialId`) into refreshOAuthTokens' `userId` parameter, so the sync endpoint is told the wrong Cal.com user id.
suggestions.suggestionContent: refreshOAuthTokens' third parameter is `userId: number | null` and is sent to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT as `calcomUserId` (packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:3,11). All eight other call sites changed in this PR pass `credential.userId`; this one passes `credentialId`, the credential row's primary key. When app credential sharing is enabled, the sync endpoint therefore receives a credential id instead of the Cal.com user id and will return tokens for the wrong or a nonexistent user. Pass `credential.userId` here like the other integrations.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Docblock describes both appData.type and appData.appId as "the app slug" even though type is the credential type, a different value.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The docblock documents both `@param appData.type` and `@param appData.appId` as "the app slug", but they are distinct values written to distinct credential fields: `type` is the credential type (e.g. "google_calendar") while `appId` is the app slug (e.g. "google-calendar"). A caller reading this doc would pass the slug for both and store a wrong credential type. Document `type` as the app/credential type.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Decryption falls back to an empty-string encryption key when CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY is missing instead of failing fast.
suggestions.suggestionContent: Decryption falls back to an empty-string encryption key when CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY is missing instead of failing fast.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: encodeOAuthState just echoes the incoming `state` query param (which doesn't exist at flow initiation), so teamId/returnTo are never encoded into the OAuth state.
suggestions.suggestionContent: encodeOAuthState is a copy of decodeOAuthState: it JSON.parses the incoming `req.query.state` and re-stringifies the identical value. Its callers are the OAuth *initiation* handlers (googlecalendar/api/add.ts:36, office365calendar/api/add.ts:18, zoomvideo/api/add.ts:23, larkcalendar/api/add.ts:21, salesforce/api/add.ts:25, hubspot/api/add.ts:27, zoho-bigin/api/add.ts:27, zohocrm/api/_getAdd.ts:15, office365video/api/add.ts:18), which call it to BUILD the state for the authorization URL — at that point there is no `state` query param, so the function returns undefined and teamId/returnTo are never encoded. The callback's decodeOAuthState then finds no teamId, so createOAuthAppCredential's team-install branch can never run and the returnTo redirect is lost. The encoder should construct the state from the initiation query params (teamId, returnTo) instead of echoing req.query.state.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Unguarded prisma.update in the new catch/else retry paths throws P2025 when the reminder was concurrently deleted, crashing the cron handler and aborting the rest of the batch.
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The retryCount increment inside the catch block (and the identical one in the else branch at lines 179-186) calls prisma.workflowReminder.update on reminder.id without guarding against the row having been deleted after the initial findMany. WHY: WorkflowReminder rows are hard-deleted outside this handler — deleteScheduledSMSReminder (smsReminderManager.ts:251) deletes by id on booking cancel/reschedule, and an overlapping cron run's deleteMany can also remove rows — while this loop is suspended awaiting Twilio/prisma calls. prisma.update on a missing row throws P2025; thrown from inside the catch block it is unhandled, so it propagates out of the for loop, returns a 500, and aborts scheduling of every remaining reminder in the batch. Before this PR the catch only logged, so a concurrently deleted reminder could never crash the run. HOW: Wrap the failure-path updates in their own try/catch (or use updateMany so a missing row is a no-op), e.g. `try { await prisma.workflowReminder.update(...) } catch {}` inside the catch, keeping the original console.log.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The retryCount>1 cleanup branch is not scoped to method:SMS, so the SMS cron would delete email/WhatsApp reminders if they ever carry a retryCount.
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The second OR branch of the deleteMany (`retryCount: { gt: 1 }`) omits the `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` filter that the first branch has, so this SMS cron deletes WorkflowReminder rows of any method (EMAIL, WHATSAPP) once retryCount exceeds 1. WHY: Today the only writer of WorkflowReminder.retryCount is this file and it only processes SMS reminders, so no non-SMS row can currently have retryCount > 0 — but the query contradicts its own intent ("delete all scheduled sms reminders") and any future code path (or data backfill) that increments retryCount on email/WhatsApp reminders would cause the SMS cron to silently delete those reminders without their provider-side messages ever being cancelled. HOW: Add `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` to the retryCount branch so both OR branches are SMS-scoped.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The catch block now awaits a Prisma update that can itself throw, breaking the previous guarantee that one failing reminder never aborts the batch.
suggestions.suggestionContent: Before this PR, the catch block only logged, so a failure on one reminder was swallowed and the for-loop always continued to the next reminder. Now both the else branch (lines 178-187) and the catch block (lines 189-197) await prisma.workflowReminder.update(...). If that write rejects — e.g. Prisma P2025 'record to update not found' when an overlapping cron run's widened deleteMany (the new unguarded `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` OR-branch at lines 38-42 deletes rows regardless of method, scheduled flag, or scheduledDate) removes the reminder mid-processing — the exception escapes the catch (the else-branch failure triggers the catch, which retries the same failing update and throws again). The entire loop aborts: every remaining unscheduled SMS reminder in the batch is skipped for this cron run and the endpoint returns 500 instead of 200. The per-reminder failure-isolation contract the caller relied on is gone. Wrap the retry-count increments in their own try/catch (or use updateMany / a .catch()) so a failed retry-count write is logged but never propagates.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The catch block's own prisma update can throw, turning handled per-reminder failures into an unhandled exception that aborts the whole batch.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: retryCount is updated with a stale read-modify-write (`reminder.retryCount + 1`) instead of an atomic increment, and under overlapping cron runs this can corrupt state — including deletion of a successfully scheduled reminder.
suggestions.suggestionContent:
Both new updates write `retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1` using the value snapshot at findMany time (line 60). If cron invocations overlap, two runs read the same N and both write N+1 (lost increment). A worse interleaving: run A marks the row retryCount=2 while run B marks scheduled=true; the next run's deleteMany (`retryCount > 1`, no `scheduled` filter) then deletes a successfully scheduled reminder, orphaning the Twilio-scheduled SMS and breaking later cancellation by referenceId. Use an atomic increment and consider scoping the retry-based deletion to unscheduled rows:

```ts
data: { retryCount: { increment: 1 } }
```

and in the deleteMany: `{ scheduled: false, retryCount: { gt: 1 } }`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The comment above deleteMany still says it only deletes SMS reminders whose scheduled date has passed, but this PR added an OR branch that also deletes any reminder with retryCount > 1.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The comment on line 28 — "//delete all scheduled sms reminders where scheduled date is past current date" — no longer describes the query below it. The new OR branch (lines 38-42) also deletes every reminder with retryCount > 1, regardless of method or scheduledDate, so the comment now states only half of the deletion condition. Update the comment to mention both conditions, e.g. "//delete all scheduled sms reminders where scheduled date is past current date, and any reminders that exceeded the retry limit", so the next reader knows this query is also the retry purge.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Supplying any non-empty totpCode alongside a backup code skips password verification, turning a leaked backup code into a single-factor login credential.
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The new backup-code branch (line 131) authenticates the user solely on `credentials.backupCode` — the supplied `credentials.totpCode` is never verified in this branch, and the password check at line 121 (`if (user.password && !credentials.totpCode)`) is skipped whenever any non-empty totpCode is posted. WHY: An attacker who obtains a user's backup code (this PR explicitly encourages downloading `cal-backup-codes.txt`) but NOT their password can log in by POSTing credentials `{email, password: "anything", totpCode: "000000", backupCode: "<leaked code>"}` — the junk totpCode bypasses the password check and is never validated. Previously the password skip required a *valid* time-based TOTP (unforgeable without the secret); this PR extends the bypass to static, stealable backup codes, silently downgrading password+2FA accounts to backup-code-only single factor. HOW: Verify the password unconditionally before the second-factor branch (e.g. change line 121 to `if (user.password)`), matching disable.ts which always calls verifyPassword first; alternatively verify the totpCode in the backup-code branch too.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Backup code consumption is a non-atomic read-modify-write, so two concurrent logins can both succeed with the same single-use code.
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The authorize flow decrypts `user.backupCodes`, checks `indexOf(credentials.backupCode)`, and only then re-encrypts and persists the array with the used code nulled — a check-then-act sequence with no locking or atomic update. WHY: Two concurrent login requests presenting the same backup code both read the pre-update array, both pass the `indexOf` check, and both authenticate, violating the "Each backup code can be used exactly once" guarantee shown to users in the UI copy added by this PR; the second write also silently overwrites the first. HOW: Make consumption atomic, e.g. perform the update inside a transaction that re-reads `backupCodes` and re-validates the code is still present before nulling it (retry/abort if absent), or store codes as individual rows and consume one with `updateMany` guarded on the code value.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: `req.body.backupCode.replaceAll` is called after only a truthy check, so a non-string JSON body crashes the endpoint with an unhandled TypeError.
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: Line 48 checks only that `req.body.backupCode` is truthy before line 61 calls `req.body.backupCode.replaceAll("-", "")`; a JSON body such as `{"backupCode": {}}` or `{"backupCode": ["x"]}` passes the truthy check but has no `replaceAll` method. WHY: Any authenticated user with 2FA enabled can send a malformed body and cause an unhandled TypeError, returning a 500 (and in the login twin of this code, next-auth-options.ts:144, the same pattern exists) instead of a clean 400 — noisy error handling and a trivially triggerable crash path in a security-sensitive endpoint. HOW: Validate the type before use, e.g. `if (typeof req.body.backupCode !== "string") return res.status(400).json({ error: ErrorCode.IncorrectBackupCode });` before calling replaceAll.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The copy button calls `navigator.clipboard.writeText` without checking the Clipboard API exists, throwing a TypeError on non-HTTPS origins.
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The `backup-codes-copy` click handler calls `navigator.clipboard.writeText(...)` unconditionally; the Clipboard API is only exposed in secure contexts, so on self-hosted Cal.com instances served over plain HTTP `navigator.clipboard` is `undefined`. WHY: Clicking "Copy" on such a deployment throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'writeText')` in the handler — the success toast is never shown, nothing is copied, and an unhandled error is logged, breaking the one copy path users see right after enabling 2FA (the download path via blob URL still works). HOW: Guard the call (`if (navigator.clipboard)`) and fall back to a textarea + `document.execCommand("copy")` or surface an error toast telling the user to use Download instead.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The '2FA got enabled' assertion always passes because expect() is called on the Promise returned by isChecked(), which is always truthy.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The copy-button test only waits for a success toast that the implementation shows unconditionally, so it passes even if nothing is copied.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: The missing-backup-codes error message tells locked-out login users to 'generate them in your settings', an action the code makes impossible in that context.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The new string "missing_backup_codes" says "No backup codes found. Please generate them in your settings." but this PR wires it into the login flow (login.tsx shows it when authorize returns ErrorCode.MissingBackupCodes), where the user is locked out and cannot reach settings at all; and nothing in settings lets a user generate backup codes short of re-running full 2FA setup. The instruction is unactionable in every context where the code displays it — reword it (e.g. point to account-recovery support) or don't surface it on the login page.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Backup code verification on the login path uses non-constant-time Array.indexOf string comparison, leaking prefix-match timing information about valid backup codes.
suggestions.suggestionContent: The backup code is verified with `backupCodes.indexOf(credentials.backupCode.replaceAll("-", ""))`. `Array.prototype.indexOf` compares strings with `===`, which returns as soon as it finds a differing character — so the time this check takes depends on how many leading characters of the attacker's guess match a real backup code. Backup codes are authentication credentials (a correct one grants login with no authenticator), and this comparison runs on the unauthenticated login path, so a remote attacker can use response timing as an oracle to recover a code character-by-character; rate limiting slows this but does not remove the leak. Compare in constant time instead: decode the normalized user code and each stored code to Buffers and use `crypto.timingSafeEqual` (after an equal-length check), tracking a boolean match flag across all entries without early exit.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.oneSentenceSummary: Disable-2FA endpoint verifies backup codes with non-constant-time Array.indexOf, leaking prefix-match timing information.
suggestions.suggestionContent: Same non-constant-time comparison as the login path: `backupCodes.indexOf(req.body.backupCode.replaceAll("-", ""))` uses short-circuiting `===` string equality to verify an authentication credential, so rejection time leaks how many leading characters of the guess match a stored backup code. This endpoint is behind a session and password check, which lowers exploitability, but the credential comparison itself should still be constant time — use `crypto.timingSafeEqual` over equal-length Buffers for each stored code, without early exit.

suggestions.label: bug
